notes:
Overview: Palisade evaluating Redwood Dedicated for production-facing chat + rerank pipelines. Focus area: autoscaling behaviour under bursty flash claims traffic and reserved GPU planning to meet latency SLOs.

Technical/requirements highlights:
- Primary workloads: conversational chat (avg 300 tokens), reranking (short sequences for reordering recommendations), nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Throughput: baseline sustained 200 req/s for chat across two availability zones with ability to handle 1k req/s 5-minute spikes without exceeding p95 latency SLA.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 140ms for chat on 8B-class model; p99 target 350ms. Rerank paths tighter: p95 < 100ms.
- Reserved GPUs request: initial commit 16x H100-80GB equivalent, split 10 / 6 across primary/secondary AZs. Expect growth to 24 in 12 months.
- Warm pools: prefer warm-pool policy per shard with target of 1 warm replica per 10 shards; warm startup scripts to pre-warm KV caches and model weights. Warm-up target < 90s.
- Autoscaling policy: hybrid predictive + reactive. Predictive uses traffic calendar (claims cycles) + learned diurnal model. Reactive triggers: sustained GPU utilization > 72% for 45s or queue length > 50 requests. Scale-up goal: new shard available for routing within 45s; scale-down: drain for min 10 minutes with graceful cache handover to avoid cold-cache misses.
- Queueing/backpressure: per-shard bounded queue; soft-limit at 120ms wait, hard-limit at 250ms then apply token-shed with informative 429 + advisory header. For non-critical reranking, configure fallback to smaller quantized model on same fleet.
- Fallbacks: auto-fallback to quantized 4-bit model variant or Redwood Hosted for overflow; require per-request telemetry tagging when fallback used.
- SLA asks: 99.9% availability for dedicated fleet, credits for monthly p95 misses exceeding agreed thresholds; request explicit clause forbidding forced single-region termination without 60-day notice and runbook for multi-region failover.
- Observability: need per-GPU token/s, per-model KV hit-rate, warm-pool fill ratio, queue latency distribution, autoscaler event logs, and a daily digest for SRE team.
- Cost sensitivity: looking for 25%+ discount on 12/24 month reserved commits; interested in Optimize consultancy for batching and quantization plans.
- Security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 compliance required; retention of audit logs 18 months.

Recent timeline (CRM entries):
- 2026-01-15: Lead created (AE Lina).
- 2026-01-28: Initial discovery call 8: capacity needs flagged, asked for sizing template.
- 2026-02-10: Architecture workshop w/ SE Daniel; discussed warm pool/kv cache strategies and rerank latency constraints.
- 2026-02-25: POC plan agreed (2-week synthetic + 24h stealth run with production traces).
- 2026-03-03: Baseline POC run 8 results: p95 ~160ms with many shards cold; warm replicas improved p95 to ~130ms. Observed autoscaler delayed scale-up during sudden 5x burst.
- 2026-03-08: Redwood infra adjusted scale-up threshold and prefetch warm-up script deployed. Second run scheduled.
- 2026-03-11: Legal asked for SLA redlines and termination notice period update.

Open actions/next steps:
- Redwood: perform extended 6-hour POC with scheduled bursts that mimic claims peaks; instrument warm-pool heatmaps and autoscaler decision traces. Deliver tuning recommendations.
- Customer: share production traffic histogram for claims window and confirm egress limits for VPC peering.
- Finance: prepare 12mo vs 24mo pricing scenarios with reserved GPU tiers and breach credit table.

AE notes:
- Strong desire to avoid oscillation in scale-down; recommend minimum warm pool floor and longer drain windows.
- High chance for multi-year commit if p95 consistently under 140ms with documented incident response.
- Potential upsell: Optimize engagement + dedicated SLA with faster legal turn-around.
